messages:
incidentbot: :rotating_light: PagerDuty alert: HIGH - hosted-inference - model-serving-500s fired for scope=prod-us-west. Escalation policy 'prod-inference-escalation' triggered. Primary on-call (maria (oncall)) notified.

pagerduty: Incident 2026-03-15T02:01:07Z created (ID: PD-98765). No ack within 2m -> will escalate to secondary in 1m. Links: https://pagerduty.example/PD-98765

maria (oncall): ugh, phone on silent. seeing a ton of 502s in Grafana for /v1/generate in us-west.

kate (eng-sre): copying graphs — spike at 02:00UTC, p50 p95 both jump, errors ~30% of requests for short seq lengths.

ajay (secondary): I'm 2 min out, will join. can someone paste the most recent deploy?

jordan: latest deploy at 01:49UTC by ci-bot -> inference-runtime v3.4.1-rc; rollout completed 01:52. No config flags changed in the last 6h.

maria (oncall): acked. looking at controller logs now.

maria (oncall): seeing repeated OOM messages on model-worker-3, restarting pod.

kate (eng-sre): logs: ```
model-worker-3 stderr: RuntimeError: CUDA out of memory when allocating KV cache
2026-03-15T02:01:22Z worker-restart
```

ajay (secondary): if OOM across pool, could be memory regression from v3.4.1-rc quantization path. can we pin to v3.4.0?

ops-manager: manager escalation fired (ops-manager) — paging to phone. if primary/secondary cannot mitigate, consider emergency rollback.

maria (oncall): trying quick mitigation: cordon worker-3 and scale up replica count for model-pool to 8 (was 4) to spread KV cache.

kate (eng-sre): scaling command: `kubectl scale deployment/model-pool --replicas=8 -n prod-us-west`

jordan: live traffic shows CPU on new nodes is fine but memory still high on each pod; suspect memory footprint per process increased.

ajay (secondary): starting a canary failover to eu-central for non-authenticated /gen traffic for low-latency customers to reduce load on us-west. will update routing.

maria (oncall): rolling restart complete for worker-3, still seeing 5xx but decreasing from 30% -> 12% over last 2m.

pagerduty: Escalation note: secondary (ajay (secondary)) acked at 5901234580. Manager escalated at 5901234620 because incident persisted.

kate (eng-sre): quick note: customer-visible errors seem limited to model X large (seq > 2048). small models unaffected. adding a temporary reject rule for huge sequences from public API.

maria (oncall): applied rate limit patch: `nginx lua` rule -> drop seq > 2048 for model X with 429.

jordan: logs after patch: error rate dropped to ~6%, latency p95 improved.

ops-manager: I called the primary manager on mobile, manager confirmed they are awake and on the bridge.

maria (oncall): long-term action: rolling back inference-runtime to v3.4.0 on prod-us-west; starting rollback now.

kate (eng-sre): rollback plan snippet: ```bash
# quick rollback
kubectl set image deployment/model-worker model-worker=registry/redwood/inference:v3.4.0 -n prod-us-west
# watch pods
kubectl rollout status deployment/model-worker -n prod-us-west
```

ajay (secondary): note: PD escalation window and mobile DND interaction caused delay. filing PD policy tweak ticket to extend primary ack window to 4m when DND is detected.

maria (oncall): rollback completed at 02:10UTC, monitoring. 5xx now under 1.5% and trending down.

pagerduty: PD Incident PD-98765 status: acknowledged -> resolved (auto-resolve at 02:12UTC).

maria (oncall): marking incident as mitigated, will create postmortem. immediate customer impact: several enterprise customers in APAC and US-W reporting 502s for model X large between 02:00-02:12UTC. estimated affected requests ~18k, peak error rate 30%.

ops-manager: good triage. action items: 1) postmortem with timeline + root cause (assign to kate), 2) add PD policy tweak (assign to ajay), 3) add regression test for memory footprint during RCs (assign to jordan).

kate (eng-sre): I'll own the postmortem. collecting logs and perf profiles now.

ajay (secondary): filing PD policy ticket: https://tracker.example/RED-5123

maria (oncall): thanks all. follow-up: restore replicas to baseline after we confirm stability. leaving this thread open for notes. :white_check_mark:
